reasoning_summary: Selected features prioritize stable, interpretable credit risk signals with zero missingness and broad coverage across key semantic groups: external scores, application demographics, bureau credit history and indebtedness, installment repayment behavior, previous application behavior, and property/building characteristics. Redundancy is controlled by selecting representative aggregates with clear credit-risk meaning and avoiding tail-dominated or sparse features. Features with potential leakage or operational brittleness are excluded. The list balances durable behavioral signals, capacity, exposure, delinquency, and customer history, suitable for stable out-of-time generalization and defensible scorecard review.
selection_principles: Prioritize features with zero missingness and broad coverage for stability
Select interpretable features representing durable credit risk concepts
Control redundancy by choosing representative aggregates within semantic groups
Exclude features prone to leakage, operational brittleness, or sparse tail dominance
Ensure broad semantic coverage across external scores, bureau data, repayment behavior, and application info
Favor features with stable, durable repayment and indebtedness signals
Prefer features defensible in scorecard and regulatory reviews
